questions.question: What is the primary function of data collector jobs in Performance Analytics?

options.text: To create new indicators automatically
To take periodic snapshots of process tables and store them in Scores and Snapshots tables
To export dashboard data to external systems
To validate indicator configurations

explanation.correct: The Data Collector is the engine that takes periodic snapshots of your process tables and stores them in the Scores and Snapshots tables.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Data collector jobs collect scores; indicators must be created manually or through other means.
Data collection is for internal score collection, not external export.
Validation is done through diagnostics, not data collector jobs.

source.excerpt: Data collector is the engine that takes periodic snapshots of your process tables and stores them in the Scores and Snapshots tables.

questions.question: What is the recommended relationship between a data collector job's schedule and an indicator source's frequency?

options.text: The job should run more frequently than the indicator frequency
The job schedule should match the indicator source frequency
The job should run less frequently than the indicator frequency
There is no relationship between job schedule and indicator frequency

explanation.correct: Usually set a job schedule to match the frequency in the indicator source.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Running more frequently than needed wastes resources without collecting new data.
Running less frequently would miss collection periods defined in the indicator source.
The job schedule should align with indicator frequency for optimal data collection.

source.excerpt: Usually set a job schedule to match the frequency in the indicator source.

questions.question: Which type of data collection job should be run only once to populate empty indicators?

options.text: Daily data collection job
Historical data collection job
Automated data collection job
Scheduled data collection job

explanation.correct: You can set up jobs that run manually, such as historical jobs, which you run only when collecting data for a new indicator.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Daily jobs run on a schedule, not as one-time historical collection.
Automated jobs are scheduled to run regularly, not for one-time historical population.
Scheduled jobs run repeatedly; historical jobs are run once to backfill data.

source.excerpt: You can also set up jobs that run manually, such as historical jobs, which you run only when collecting data for a new indicator.

questions.question: Which two actions should be performed in the 'Collect data' phase of PA implementation? (Choose two.)

options.text: Schedule and activate data collector jobs
Create dashboard visualizations
Run historical data collector jobs as a one-off
Define business goals and measurements

explanation.correct: In the Collect data phase, collection jobs need to be configured to run with the desired frequency and activated, and historical data collector jobs should be run as a one-off to populate empty indicators.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Dashboard creation is part of the 'Share results' phase, not data collection.
Defining goals is part of the 'Plan and Prepare' phase, not data collection.

source.excerpt: Collect data: Collection jobs need to be configured to run with the desired frequency and activated. Schedule and activate data collector jobs. Run historical data collector jobs as a one-off to populate empty indicators.

questions.question: What happens when one data collection job generates scores for multiple indicators?

options.text: Each indicator receives a separate job
This is not possible; each job collects for one indicator only
One job usually generates scores for multiple indicators that use the same indicator source
The job fails due to conflicts

explanation.correct: One job usually generates scores for multiple indicators that use the same indicator source.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Jobs are not automatically separated; one job can handle multiple indicators with the same source.
A single job can collect for multiple indicators sharing an indicator source.
Multiple indicators per job is normal behavior, not a conflict.

source.excerpt: One job usually generates scores for multiple indicators that use the same indicator source.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Performance Analytics diagnostics?

options.text: To schedule data collection jobs
To identify and diagnose configuration issues using predefined scripts
To create new indicator sources
To export collected scores to external systems

explanation.correct: Performance Analytics diagnostics identify and diagnose configuration issues using predefined scripts that examine the database for invalid records and provide suggestions to resolve issues.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Job scheduling is done in the PA Admin Console, not diagnostics.
Indicator sources are created manually, not through diagnostics.
Export functionality is separate from diagnostics.

source.excerpt: Identify and diagnose configuration issues using predefined scripts that examine the database for invalid records and provide suggestions to resolve issues.

questions.question: Which three levels of logging does Performance Analytics provide for data collection jobs?

options.text: Job events, job logs, and job log details
Error logs, warning logs, and info logs
Collection logs, processing logs, and storage logs
System logs, application logs, and audit logs

explanation.correct: Performance Analytics provides three levels of log: job events (which jobs executed), job logs (overview of each job), and job log details (what happened in each step).

wrongAnswers.explanation: PA does not categorize logs by severity level in this way.
These are not the three PA log levels.
These are general ServiceNow log categories, not PA-specific levels.

questions.question: What does the nested collection optimization do in the classic data collector?

options.text: Collects data for nested indicator sources in parallel
Creates one object per indicator instead of duplicates for every breakdown and element
Nests breakdown scores within indicator score records
Processes child domains before parent domains

explanation.correct: Nested collection replaces flat mapping to reduce redundant objects. Instead of creating identical indicator objects for every breakdown and element, only one object is created for the indicator.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Nested collection is about memory optimization, not parallel processing.
It reduces redundant objects in memory, not score record nesting.
It has nothing to do with domain processing order.

questions.question: What is the default value of the flush snapshot count property (com.snc.pa.dc.flush_snapshot_count) in Performance Analytics?

explanation.correct: The flush_snapshot_count property defaults to 1000. It controls the maximum number of PA snapshots stored in memory before offloading them to the database.

wrongAnswers.explanation: 100 is not the default value.
500 is not the default value.
5000 is not the default value.

questions.question: When a data collection job processes an indicator source condition that includes 'Today', how is 'Today' interpreted?

options.text: Relative to the current system date
Relative to the period for which the data collection job is executed
Relative to the job's scheduled start time
Relative to UTC midnight

explanation.correct: If the indicator source specifies Today in one of the conditions, Today is considered relative to the period for which the data collection job is executed, not the current date.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Today is relative to the collection period, not the current system date.
It is relative to the collection period, not the scheduled start time.
It uses the collection period, not UTC midnight.

questions.question: An administrator notices that a data collection job's statistics show 'errors: 5'. Where should they look first for detailed troubleshooting information?

options.text: System logs → All
Performance Analytics → Admin Console → Troubleshoot
Data collection job → Job log details
Platform Analytics → Diagnostics

explanation.correct: Job log details describe what happened in each step of an executed job and provide the most granular troubleshooting information for collection errors.

wrongAnswers.explanation: System logs are too broad; PA-specific log details are more useful.
The Admin Console Troubleshoot panel is good for overview but job log details provide step-by-step information.
Platform Analytics Diagnostics run predefined tests, not job-specific troubleshooting.

questions.question: Which two statements about the map/reduce function during PA data collection are true? (Choose two.)

options.text: It deletes previous scores for indicators before processing new records
It processes records sequentially without tracking memory usage
It logs the percentage of records processed and result object size
It can only process a maximum of 10,000 records per run

explanation.correct: During data collection, the map/reduce function first deletes previous scores for the indicators and breakdowns, then processes each record while logging progress percentage and memory usage (result object size).

wrongAnswers.explanation: The map/reduce function does track and log memory usage during processing.
The optimized collector can handle over 10 million records; there is no 10,000 limit.

questions.question: What does the com.snc.pa.dc.use_hashcode_for_distinct property control?

options.text: Whether distinct indicators use hash-based deduplication for score storage
Whether count distinct aggregations are stored as a hashcode instead of separate values
Whether distinct breakdown elements are hashed for faster lookup
Whether the data collector uses hash partitioning for parallel processing

explanation.correct: The use_hashcode_for_distinct property stores count distinct aggregations as a hashcode instead of as separate values, improving efficiency. It defaults to true.

wrongAnswers.explanation: This property specifically affects count distinct aggregations, not general deduplication.
It affects aggregation storage, not breakdown element lookup.
It is not related to parallel processing or partitioning.

questions.question: An administrator is reviewing the data collection job log. Which two pieces of information are shown at the start of the collection job? (Choose two.)

options.text: The domain of the Run As user
The total number of records to be processed
Whether scores, text index, or both are being collected
The estimated completion time

explanation.correct: The job log starts by showing the domain of the Run As user and what is being collected (scores, text index, or both), along with the optimization property settings.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The total record count is shown during processing, not at the start.
Estimated completion time is not logged at the start of collection.

questions.question: What happens to batch inserts of scores when nested collection is enabled in the classic data collector?

options.text: Batch inserts are automatically optimized
Batch inserts of scores are not supported with nested collection
Batch inserts are doubled in size for efficiency
Batch inserts are queued and processed after nested collection completes

explanation.correct: When using nested collection, batch inserts of scores are not supported. This is a trade-off for the reduced memory usage that nested collection provides.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Batch inserts are not supported, not optimized, with nested collection.
Batch inserts cannot be used at all with nested collection.
Batch inserts are disabled entirely, not queued.
